extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, newsroom editors, visual journalists, and media organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and ethical guidance for producing and distributing journalistic images that accurately represent subjects and events, including rules on manipulation, staging, and synthetic imagery. Emphasizes obligations for photographers, editors, and institutions (including government accounts) to preserve trust and the historical record.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deceptive alteration of photographs (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The content of a photograph must not be altered in any way that deceives the public.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPPA’s Code of Ethics forbids altering photographic content to deceive; the integrity of photographic images is essential to public trust and to the historical record. Altering editorial content in ways that misrepresent subjects or events undermines that trust and is incompatible with professional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual accuracy as fundamental to photojournalism
rubrics_metrics.description: “Visual accuracy is fundamental to photojournalism’s role in informing the public and preserving the historical record.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and truthfulness are described as core to the credibility of visual reporting; photographers and outlets must prioritize truthful depiction over aesthetics or persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit alterations that change substance, distort context, or convey false impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: “Alterations that change the substance of a scene, distort context, or convey a false impression ... violate the basic ethical standards of our profession and weaken public trust in visual media.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any editing that materially changes what occurred or the context in which it occurred is ethically impermissible. This includes edits that produce a different narrative, alter subject expressions/conditions, or remove/insert elements that change meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special prohibition on manipulation when distributed by official government channels
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPPA highlights that manipulation “especially when distributed by official government channels, violate the basic ethical standards ... and weaken public trust.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images disseminated by public officials or government accounts carry heightened responsibility; government use of manipulated imagery is particularly corrosive to public trust and should be condemned and corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not stage events while depicting them as spontaneous
rubrics_metrics.description: As stated by the Writing With Light initiative: “neither alterations to a photograph that mislead the public, nor staging events while depicting them as spontaneous, are acceptable in journalism.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staging scenes (posing subjects, arranging events) and then presenting them as candid or spontaneous is unethical. If staging occurs, transparency is required; otherwise the image should not be presented as journalistic documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish photorealistic AI-generated images as real photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: “Nor should one publish a photorealistic synthetic image made by artificial intelligence and pretend that it is an actual photograph.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photorealistic synthetic images must not be passed off as authentic photographs; practitioners should label or otherwise disclose synthetic content and avoid presenting AI-generated imagery as documentary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for public officials and institutions to uphold highest standards of visual integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPPA “call[s] on all public officials and institutions to uphold the highest standards of visual integrity.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond individual practitioners, institutions and officials are expected to adopt and enforce policies that prevent deceptive image use, issue corrections when misuse occurs, and maintain transparency in visual communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to training, advocacy, and enforcement against manipulated imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: NPPA will “continue to work with partners in the journalism and press freedom community to reinforce ethical standards, provide training and resources for professionals, and resist efforts to normalize manipulated imagery in public discourse.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional organizations should provide education, resources, and advocacy to prevent normalization of manipulation; newsrooms should train staff, adopt clear policies, and enforce consequences for deceptive image practices.
